items.title: Is QCOM Stock a Buy as Auto and AI Growth Offset Handset Weakness?

items.title: Qualcomm Q3 Results Put Auto Growth and Handset Weakness in Focus
items.summary: Qualcomm's Q3 revenue beat was offset by an earnings miss as record auto growth contrasted with handset weakness and continued margin pressure.

items.title: Formula One’s Drive to Capture American Eyeballs Makes the Stock a Buy
items.summary: From Monte Carlo to Milan, the world of F1 has long been dripping with glamour, making stars out of drivers like Michael Schumacher and Lewis Hamilton, who are outshone only by the supercars themselves.  “From 1950 until about 2016, it was pretty badly run,” says Markus Hansen, a portfolio manager at Vontobel Asset Management, which owns  Liberty Media Series C Liberty Formula One  shares.  “In 2017, when Liberty Media took over Formula One, they brought a proper approach to running the business…to turning sports assets into viable financial businesses.”

items.title: QCOM Falls 30.6% in 3 Months as Handset Risks Challenge Auto Growth
items.summary: Qualcomm's 30.6% slide reflects handset weakness and margin pressure, even as automotive growth and data center targets broaden its revenue mix.

items.title: Prediction: Apple Is Entering Its Most Important Product Cycle in Years
items.summary: Apple is stacking catalysts at a pace the market has not seen in years, and the collision of new silicon, a redesigned iPhone lineup, and a long-awaited Siri AI reveal sets up a moment where getting the call wrong carries serious cost.

items.title: The Upside Case For Qualcomm Stock Now Carries Purchase Orders
items.summary: Qualcomm's non-handset business is inflecting fast enough that management expects it to replace the revenue Apple is taking away, and the first proof of that arrives in the December quarter.
